citeAs: Awadalla, A., Xue, L., Lo, O., Shu, M., Lee, H., Guha, E., Jordan, M., Shen, S., Awadalla, M., Savarese, S., Xiong, C., Xu, R., Choi, Y., Schmidt, L. (2024). MINT-1T: Scaling Open-Source Multimodal Data by 10x: A Multimodal Dataset with One Trillion Tokens. arXiv.
creator: Anas Awadalla, Le Xue, Oscar Lo, Manli Shu, Hannah Lee, Etash Guha, Matt Jordan, Sheng Shen, Mohamed Awadalla, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, Ran Xu, Yejin Choi, Ludwig Schmidt (University of Washington; Salesforce Research; Stanford University; University of Texas at Austin; University of California, Berkeley)
description: MINT-1T is an open-source multimodal interleaved pre-training dataset containing free-form sequences of images and text. It includes HTML, PDF, and ArXiv documents and comprises one trillion text tokens and 3.4 billion images.
name: MINT-1T
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that text quality classifier models can favor text from certain demographics, so MINT-1T follows prior work in avoiding model-based text quality classifiers. It also notes that because the data comes from the public web, harmful, confidential, personally identifying, or sensitive content may still be present despite filtering.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected from CommonCrawl WARC dumps for HTML documents, CommonCrawl WAT dumps for PDF documents, and ArXiv source/S3 buckets for ArXiv documents. HTML documents were parsed from DOM trees, PDFs were downloaded and parsed with PyMuPDF, and ArXiv documents were built from LaTeX source using TexSoup, followed by filtering, NSFW removal, PII masking, and deduplication.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: For HTML images, the pipeline discards non-retrievable image links and removes documents that have no valid image links. In the released dataset, the full data relies on external image URLs and the paper states there are no guarantees these URLs will remain available over time due to link rot.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of HTML documents and image URLs from CommonCrawl WARC dumps, PDF links from CommonCrawl WAT dumps, and ArXiv LaTeX source/PDF-linked content. The released dataset provides document text plus image URLs for HTML, and text plus PDF URL and image reference numbers for PDFs and ArXiv.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The data was collected from January 2024 to June 2024. The dataset includes web data from 2013 to 2024, with HTML documents from CommonCrawl dumps spanning May 2017 to April 2024 and PDF documents from February 2023 to April 2024 dumps.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Document analysis, Software Collection
rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes limitations in PDF parsing: images may sometimes not be detected, and reading order can be extracted incorrectly for arbitrary layouts, such as reading across column boundaries. It also notes that the dataset is not self-contained because it relies on external image URLs that may disappear over time, and recommends against using the dataset for models that ingest or generate personally identifying information or for military applications.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Post-collection manipulations include filtering out non-English documents, removing documents with no images or more than thirty images, removing documents with NSFW URL substrings, discarding PDFs over 50MB or over 50 pages, excluding PDF pages with no text, masking email addresses and IP addresses, removing images based on size and aspect-ratio thresholds, removing documents containing a single NSFW image, and performing paragraph, document, and image deduplication.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing includes DOM parsing for HTML, PDF reading-order extraction by clustering text blocks and anchoring images by bounding-box proximity, and ArXiv LaTeX parsing with figure-tag extraction and cleanup that removes imports, bibliography, tables, and citation tags. The pipeline also applies FastText language identification with a 0.65 confidence threshold, RefinedWeb and MassiveText text-quality filtering, NSFW filtering, PII anonymization for emails and IPs, and Bloom-filter-based text deduplication plus SHA256 image deduplication.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors state they will actively respond to issues in MINT-1T and maintain the dataset. Updates will be communicated through the README on the HuggingFace dataset page, an erratum will be present on the README, older versions can be found through Git history, and contributions will be accepted through HuggingFace pull requests.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper discusses the risk of exposing harmful content from the web and describes efforts to filter personally identifiable information and NSFW content. It also states that inappropriate uses include training models that ingest or generate personally identifying information and military applications.
rai:dataUseCases: MINT-1T was created for pre-training large multimodal models that process interleaved images and text. The paper also states it could be used for other training objectives like generating interleaved image-text sequences and for building multimodal document retrieval systems.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: FastText language identification model, PyMuPDF for PDF parsing, TexSoup for parsing ArXiv LaTeX, an NSFW image detector from Gant Laborde, datatrove text quality filters, and the Big Friendly Filter (BFF) for deduplication.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset may contain public-web content about individuals and sensitive information present on the web, including images of individuals and text about specific individuals. The paper specifically discusses masking email addresses and IP addresses and notes that sensitive data such as race or ethnic origins, sexual orientations, religious beliefs, political opinions, locations, financial or health data may be present if found on the public web.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: dataset is unlabeled pre-training data; paper states no label or target is associated with each instance
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: no human annotators or crowdworkers were involved in data collection
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: paper does not describe human annotation agreement or validation because the dataset is not human-annotated
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: no annotation platform is used; paper states no crowdworkers or contractors were involved
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: dataset is not human-labeled; no annotation protocol described
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: paper does not describe imputing or filling missing values
